newsitem.title: ITALY: BASKETBALL-PEN PICTURES OF OLYMPIAKOS AND BARCELONA.
newsitem.headline: BASKETBALL-PEN PICTURES OF OLYMPIAKOS AND BARCELONA.

text.p: Following are penpix of leading players and assessments of main strengths and weaknesses of Olympiakos and Barcelona who meet in the European basketball final on Thursday:

Strengths: Playmaker David Rivers is a potential match-winner at any level. Top-scorer with 28 points in Tuesday's semifinal victory over Ljubljana. Famed frontline of Dragan Tarlac and Panayotis Fasoulas are masters on a good day of scoring, collecting rebounds and blocking.
Weaknesses: Can be inconsistent; score less frequently with three-pointers from outside the D.

Dragan Tarlac - A Serb Chicago Bulls hopeful, among the strongest forwards in Europe. Most opponents have trouble guarding him. "Once he gets the ball inside the D the chances are he will score even if two opponents try to stop him. He is a rare talent," FIBA general secretary Borislav Stankovic said recently.
Panayotis Fasoulas - A veteran in European play and Greece's best blocker. Nicknamed the "Spider" he covers the baskets with his long hands and is rarely beaten in one-to-one encounters inside the D.
George Sigalas - Probably Europe's best defender but fouls a lot. On a good day he scores three-pointers and can turn a match around with his explosive style.

David Rivers - The club's fast American playmaker known for his end-to-end runs, perfect assists and shots from outside the D. Can get carried away shooting while he should pass and can be lazy in defence.
Strengths: Have improved as the season has progressed thanks largely to the arrival of Serb guard Sasha Djordjevic.
Weaknesses: Over-reliance on occasions on Djordjevic. By no means invincible as early season record shows.

Aleksandar ('Sasha') Djordjevic - Joined the side from Teamsystem Bologna in January after Russian forward Andrei Fetissov failed to come up with the goods and has revolutionised Barcelona's play. Strong in assists and a fine triple-shot man. Very influential and top scored in Tuesday's semifinal win over Villeurbanne with 17 points.
Arturas Karnishovas - The Lithuanian is good from the triple shot line. Often fragile at key moments and failed to live up to expectations in last year's dramatic European defeat by Panathinaikos.

Andres Jimenez - The veteran captain has been present at all five previous Final Fours played by Barcelona since 1989. Power forward, has regained importance in the team because of injury problems in the centre position. Strong close to the hoop and scored a useful 16 points in Tuesday's win over Villeurbanne.

Roberto Duenas - Shaking off the image of uncoordinated giant with recent performances in which he has successfully disrupted the shooting strategies of opponents. A good rebound man. Duenas's recently-renewed contract prevents him going to any team except those in the NBA -- where he is already arousing interest.
